slides.heading: How Fusion Energy Finally Works
slides.body: The science powering the stars — and soon, our cities

slides.heading: What Is Nuclear Fusion?
slides.body: Fusion is the process of fusing two light atomic nuclei — usually hydrogen isotopes — into a heavier nucleus, releasing enormous energy. It's the same reaction that powers the Sun and every star in the universe.

slides.heading: Fusion vs. Fission
slides.body: Unlike fission (splitting atoms, used in today's nuclear plants), fusion produces far more energy per unit of fuel and generates no long-lived radioactive waste. The main byproduct is helium — an inert, harmless gas.

slides.heading: The Fuel: Deuterium & Tritium
slides.body: Fusion reactors use deuterium (extracted from seawater) and tritium (bred from lithium). Earth has enough deuterium to power civilization for billions of years, making fusion's fuel supply essentially limitless.

slides.heading: The Big Challenge: Plasma Confinement
slides.body: Fusion requires temperatures exceeding 100 million°C — hotter than the Sun's core. At these temperatures, fuel becomes plasma that must be contained using powerful magnetic fields, typically in a donut-shaped device called a tokamak.

slides.heading: The Ignition Breakthrough
slides.body: In December 2022, the National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition for the first time — producing more energy from the reaction than the laser energy delivered to the fuel. This milestone proved net energy gain is physically possible.

slides.heading: ITER: The Global Bet
slides.body: ITER, under construction in France with 35 participating nations, is the world's largest tokamak. It aims to produce 500 MW of fusion power from just 50 MW of input — a 10x energy gain — validating commercial-scale fusion.

slides.heading: Private Companies Racing Ahead
slides.body: Startups like Commonwealth Fusion, Helion, and TAE Technologies are building compact, faster reactors using high-temperature superconducting magnets and novel confinement designs — some targeting grid power by the early 2030s.

slides.heading: Why It Changes Everything
slides.body: A working fusion grid means virtually unlimited clean energy with no carbon emissions, no meltdown risk, and fuel available to every nation on Earth. It could end energy poverty and eliminate a major driver of climate change.

slides.heading: The Star in Our Grasp
slides.body: Fusion has been '30 years away' for 70 years — but the physics is now proven. The race is engineering. The era of star-powered electricity may finally be within reach.
